Distribution. The new species was recorded only from the Bamian Province in central Afghanistan: two localities on the northern slope of Koh-I Baba (or Baba) Mountain Range in the Hindu Kush mountain system (see map, Fig. 22). Comparison and remarks. The shape of claws of the new species (with ventral blade fused to dorsal blade) and genitalia (lobes of parameres hooked dorsally before apex, penis with one apical hook) are typical of the genus Calydus. However C. yaroslavi new species is very distinct from all congeners in the shape of the temples (Fig. 5), head dorsally not depressed, mandibles (Fig. 7) with external outline strongly curved inward at the apical third, longer and moniliform antennae (Fig. 11), subglobular and almost smooth pronotum (Fig. 9), distinct erect pubescence of body including pronotum and elytra (Fig. 1). Body coloration is similar only to that of C. syriacus (Fig. 4), but in latter the elytra totally lack a metallic tinge. Other Calydus species differ from the new species by the body colouration, having elytra which are totally black or with red, brown-red (Fig. 3) or bicoloured. Also, all the previously known species of Calydus are characterised by the temples progressively widened and not rounded posteriorly (Fig. 6), rather short antennae not attaining elytral base and weakly widened distally, antennae not moniliform with antennomeres closely articulated (Fig. 3, 4, 12); pronotum almost campaniform with the disc flattened or only weakly convex, integument with rather deep distinct punctuation (Fig. 3, 4, 10); legs more robust, tarsomeres shorter and in lateral view rather widened (Fig. 3, 4); body pubescence short and recumbent, pronotum and elytra with poorly visible, very short recumbent pubescence (Fig. 3, 4, 6, 10, 14). In the examined species C. semenovi and C. cf. syriacus (Fig. 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16) mandibles are narrower with external outline gradually and comparatively weakly curved inward (Fig. 8), submentum widely impressed, ventrolateral margin of pronotum not evenly merging with margin of prosternum and forming a distinct elevated suture extending beyond anterior outline of procoxal cavities, prosternum proximal to the middle with a wide obtuse elevation (Fig. 14).
